newsitem.title: USA: Cuban-American is first Dade County executive mayor.
newsitem.headline: Cuban-American is first Dade County executive mayor.

text.p: Alex Penelas, a Cuban-American Democrat, was elected the first executive mayor of Dade County Tuesday by a 57 to 43 percent margin in a racially divided contest that saw voters cross party lines.
The victory made Penelas, 34, a county commissioner, the second-most powerful public official in Florida, after Gov. Lawton Chiles.
He defeated Arthur Teele, 50, a black Republican and former chairman of the Dade County Commission, in the race for the new, non-partisan post.
With 91 percent of votes counted, Penelas was leading Teele by 58 to 42 percent, or 165,526 to 119,865 of votes cast, election officials said.
"Mi nombre es Alex Penelas," he said, speaking Spanish as he began a victory speech calling on Dade County's more than two million residents to unite across racial and party lines.
"Next time I'll say a few words in Creole as well," he added in English, referring to the native language of Dade County's large Haitian community.

Voting was sharply divided by race. WSVN, the Miami Fox television affiliate, reported that 92 percent of Hispanic voters had backed Penelas, versus only eight percent of blacks, while six percent of blacks backed Penelas, versus 94 percent for Teele.

The votes of non-hispanic whites were divided almost evenly, with 51 percent backing Penelas and 49 percent backing Teele. And voters crossed party lines to back their candidates, as Dade County's overwhelmingly Democratic African-American population backed the black Republican Teele and traditionally Republican Cuban-Americans backed the Cuban-American Democrat.

Dade County voters approved a strong mayor form of government last November, a move that will give the mayor new powers and major influence over Dade's $4 billion budget. The county had a mayor until a court-ordered reorganization in the early 1990s, but the post was mostly ceremonial.
